audit.whatIsWrong: The chart read Skill / Ornn / Ornn / Skill / Skill / Ornn / Ornn. The 1339-game packet chart is Skill / Skill / Skill / Ornn / Skill / Skill / Nasus — and the page's own whys already match the packet, not the chart, in five of seven rows.
audit.why: whys[1] says 'Still even with one point each' (Skill, rendered Ornn); whys[2] says 'his early Q stacks keep it close' (Skill, rendered Ornn); whys[3] says 'your first clear edge' (Ornn, rendered Skill); whys[5] says 'his Q is starting to stack toward parity' (Skill, rendered Ornn); whys[6] says outright 'Free-farmed Nasus out-scales you' while the chart handed row 6 to Ornn. A player reading the 2+ item row saw 'Ornn' next to a sentence telling them not to 1v1 him.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6 flipped in BOTH layers as one group -> Skill, Skill, Ornn, Skill, Nasus. Row 6 rating drops to 3/10; rows 0 and 4 already agreed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as an Ornn spike outright ('R's double knock-up ... wins the all-in or gank'), ignoring that Nasus ults on the same level.
audit.why: Fury of the Sands (120/100/80s, 400 range) gives him increased Health, Attack Range, bonus Armor and Magic Resistance, a reduced Siphoning Strike cooldown, and damages nearby enemies. Level 6 is contested, not free.
audit.corrected: Level 6 restated as a two-sided spike; breakdown.spikes now names Fury of the Sands with its 120s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Siphoning Strike, Spirit Fire, Fury of the Sands and Soul Eater were never named — the page said 'his Q', 'E shred', 'R lifesteal/size'. Only Wither was named, and always without numbers.
audit.why: Siphoning Strike (255 range, 7.5/6.5/5.5/4.5/3.5s) is an auto-attack RESET, so the wind-up — not the cast — is the cue to step back, and it only stacks if he slays the target, which is what makes denying the last-hit the whole game. Wither (700 range, 15/14/13/12/11s) decelerates Move Speed AND Attack Speed over time, so trading inside it means you can neither leave nor land the follow-up. Spirit Fire (650 range, flat 12s) reduces the Armor of anyone standing on it. Fury of the Sands does percent-health damage, which is why raw armour is not the answer to it.
audit.corrected: All five named with real ranges and cooldowns; the auto-reset tell added; the percent-health reason for not stacking armour stated instead of the vague 'ramping on-hit' claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet's stated defect: 'NO cooldown-sequencing advice anywhere'. Every reference to Wither was 'when it is down' with no duration.
audit.why: 'Wither is 15s at rank 1 and 11s maxed' turns a vague instruction into a countable window; Spirit Fire's flat 12s never changes, so it is the reliable clock in lane.
audit.corrected: Wither's 700/15s/11s, Spirit Fire's 650/12s and Fury of the Sands' 120s now appear in the cooldown block, the dos block and the trade lines.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim copies of tradeGood/tradeBad, and dontsFull[2].d ('Fall behind in scaling') was illustrated with an unrelated E-dash line.
audit.why: The don't titled 'Fall behind in scaling' is the single most important rule in this matchup and it carried text about terrain lines.
audit.corrected: That rule now explains that Fury of the Sands does percent-health damage, so armour stacking is not the answer at 2+ items.

Proposed as one atomic group of matched full+content pairs. DELIBERATELY NOT ASSERTED: Nasus's Soul Eater is only 'bonus Life Steal' in the kit text — I did not attach a number or claim anti-heal cuts it by a specific amount, though report[8] already prescribes early Grievous Wounds and that stands.
